$comment: Vendored enum surface mirrored from the AIgentFlow Go reference implementation. Regenerate / review on every flow-YAML schema change. See PARITY.md. Values here are public protocol/type names only.

qualityGate.$comment: DC-CP-8: the quality_gate: step block. on_fail 'human' exists in the Go enum but is validation-REJECTED (pending the human-task inbox), so it is NOT in onFailActions and is flagged as rejected here.

processingOperations.$comment: Pre/post-processing operation dispatch set and per-operation config keys. The key sets are PER OPERATION and must never be unioned: `asset_id` is read by binary.get/update/delete and is NOT read by binary.transform, which reads `source_asset_id`.

removedAgentSurfaces.$comment: AIgentFlow no longer runs agents of its own. executor_removed (ERROR): a step or loop sub-step whose executor scheme (text before '://', whitespace-trimmed, lower-cased) is in removedSchemes, or a top-level key in flowKeys (field = the key). agentic_param_removed (ERROR): an ai:// step or loop sub-step whose query carries ANY key of aiParams, on presence alone (null and false included); ONE finding per step, the keys sorted and joined by ', '. Only the paramScheme scheme is checked for params. A templated executor (containing templateActionOpen) is not judged. A step on a removed scheme yields ONLY executor_removed: no unknown_executor_scheme, executor-URL shape or inline-exons finding. Fields: steps.<id> and steps.<id>.loop.steps[<index>]. Not refused here: aiv://, nexus:// (alias atlas://), ai:// tools / tool_choice / autofix / content_parts / stream. The flow-level tool_discovery / discoverable_tools and the orchestrator block are orchestrator_removed (removedOrchestratorSurfaces). Messages fill %s (the step id as written in the finding, then the scheme or the key list).
removedAgentSurfaces.schemeMessageFormat: step %q uses %s://, which AIgentFlow no longer runs: its own agent chains were removed
removedAgentSurfaces.paramsMessageFormat: step %q sets %s on ai://: AIgentFlow's own agent loop (agentic mode) was removed, so these parameters no longer exist
removedAgentSurfaces.flowKeyMessageFormat: the flow-level key %q belonged to a removed agent surface and is no longer read
removedAgentSurfaces.suggestion: Rebuild the step: a tool-using agent becomes nexus://agent/run (agent: "@org/name", prompt, capabilities); one tool becomes nexus://capability/<ref>; a plain prompt becomes ai://<provider>/chat or a prompt-only aiv://<org>/<name>. A nexus:// step acts as the person responsible for the run: who started it, who last saved its schedule or webhook trigger, or a flow:// child's parent. What cannot be converted: a run with no person (one started by a service or key that names nobody; share links no longer exist), and a step that needs an inline .exons spec, an arbitrary MCP server URL or signals. For those, start the flow from a person, a schedule or a trigger, or use a routine in Nexus

removedSignalSurfaces.$comment: AIgentFlow 2.834.0 removed agent signals and dynamic flow modification (DFM). Since 2.838.0 the orchestrator block is refused whole (removedOrchestratorSurfaces), so nothing inside it is judged here: no finding for its enable_signals, its tool lists or its triggers. signal_removed (ERROR): stepKey on a step or loop sub-step whose scheme is stepKeyScheme (field steps.<id> / steps.<id>.loop.steps[<index>]). flow_modification_removed (ERROR): flowModificationStepKey in a step's or loop sub-step's query (any scheme). Step keys are judged on map PRESENCE (null and false included). Steps skipped: templated executors, removed schemes (removedAgentSurfaces.removedSchemes) and the schemes in stepSkipSchemes (a flow:// query carries the CHILD's inputs). Per step at most one finding of each code. removed_key_ignored (WARNING, never an error): checkpoint.pre_dfm with any non-null value (AIgentFlow wrote it into stored flows itself); pre_dfm stays in knownKeys. Order: steps by id with loop sub-steps after their parent. Reference: aigentflow.removed.signalsurfaces.go.
removedSignalSurfaces.stepKeyMessageFormat: step %q sets enable_signals: AIgentFlow's agent signals were removed in 2.834.0, so the parameter no longer exists
removedSignalSurfaces.flowModificationStepMessageFormat: step %q sets flow_modification_allowed: dynamic flow modification was removed in 2.834.0
removedSignalSurfaces.ignoredKeyMessageFormat: %s is ignored: it configured AIgentFlow's agent signals / dynamic flow modification, removed in 2.834.0. AIgentFlow may have written this key into the flow itself; the flow runs as if it were absent
removedSignalSurfaces.ignoredKeySuggestion: Remove the key; nothing reads it
removedSignalSurfaces.suggestion: Signals and dynamic flow modification were removed in 2.834.0. enable_signals: delete it; a person's answer is an async://human/<operation> step (inside a nexus://agent/run step, the Nexus approval wait asks the person). flow_modification_allowed: no replacement; declare every step the flow may run and choose between them with next: conditions

removedCampaignSurfaces.$comment: AIgentFlow 2.836.0 removed campaigns. campaign_removed (ERROR): the flow-root key flowKey with ANY non-null value (a mapping of any shape, {} included, or a scalar or list; field campaign). The block is refused whole and nothing inside it is judged: no campaign rule, retired-key, type or unknown-key finding. Steps are never judged. There is no removed_key_ignored warning for campaigns. (The tool-name and trigger arms went with the orchestrator block in 2.838.0.) Reference: aigentflow.removed.campaignsurfaces.go.
removedCampaignSurfaces.blockMessage: the flow declares a campaign: block: campaigns were removed in 2.836.0, so nothing would spawn or track its child missions
removedCampaignSurfaces.suggestion: Campaigns were removed in 2.836.0. Fan the work out inside one flow instead: a for_each step whose executor is flow://stored/<flow_id> runs the child flow once per item and hands the next step every result (.data.<step>, in item order), so a coordinator -> workers -> synthesiser campaign becomes a plan step -> a for_each over flow:// -> a synthesis step (a fixed set of different workers is next: parallel: with a rendezvous). When each worker is an agent, make the worker a nexus://agent/run step (the for_each step itself, or a step of the child flow): it runs as the person responsible for the run, and a flow:// child inherits its parent's. Delete the campaign: block

removedOrchestratorSurfaces.$comment: AIgentFlow 2.838.0 removed the orchestrator. orchestrator_removed (ERROR): (a) the flow-root key blockKey with ANY non-null value (a mapping of any shape, {} included, or a scalar or list; field orchestrator). The block is refused WHOLE and nothing inside it is judged: no exons, trigger, tool, mode, region, question-deadline, signal, campaign, type or unknown-key finding; (b) each flow-root key in discoveryKeys with any non-null value (an empty string and an empty list included; field = the key); (c) a top-level step whose next.default, or any next.conditions[].goto, is exactly nextMarker (case-sensitive): ONE finding per step, field steps.<id>, with the step id. A YAML null is absent. Loop sub-steps are not judged here (their next refuses the marker already), step query keys are never judged here (on ai:// tool_discovery / discoverable_tools are agentic_param_removed), and the step id orchestrator stays reserved. The three keys stay in knownKeys typed any, so none is an unknown key. Order: block, then discoveryKeys in order, then the steps by id. blockMessage is verbatim; flowKeyMessageFormat fills %q with the key; nextMessageFormat fills %q with the step id. Reference: aigentflow.removed.orchestratorsurfaces.go.
removedOrchestratorSurfaces.blockMessage: the flow declares an orchestrator: block: AIgentFlow's orchestrator was removed in 2.838.0, so nothing would run its agent, its triggers or its tools
removedOrchestratorSurfaces.flowKeyMessageFormat: the flow-level key %q configured the orchestrator's tool discovery, which was removed in 2.838.0, and is no longer read
removedOrchestratorSurfaces.nextMessageFormat: step %q routes next to orchestrator: the orchestrator was removed in 2.838.0, so nothing would receive the hand-over
removedOrchestratorSurfaces.suggestion: AIgentFlow no longer runs orchestrator agents (removed in 2.838.0): a coordinating agent is a nexus://agent/run step (the agent plans and calls its tools in Nexus, as the person responsible for the run); fan-out is a for_each over flow://stored/<flow_id> or nexus://agent/run; a human decision is an async://human/<operation> step, or the Nexus approval wait inside an agent step. Delete the orchestrator: block, route the steps that said next: orchestrator to a real step (or next: null), and delete the flow-level tool_discovery / discoverable_tools (give the agent its capabilities in Nexus)

executorConfigEnvScopes.$comment: executor_config may expand only the environment variables of the key it is written under. A value is a reference when it starts with referencePrefix and ends with referenceSuffix around a non-empty name. Checked fields: fields, plus every string value of extra (prefixed extraFieldPrefix in the message). A key absent from scopes has an EMPTY scope and refuses every reference. scopes is the reference's executorConfigEnvScope evaluated for every key with a non-empty scope. Reference: ValidateExecutorConfigEnvScopes (v2.597.0).

atlasExecutor.$comment: nexus://<provider>/<resource> (alias atlas://, the same rules for both spellings since AIgentFlow 2.835.0; the scheme match is exact and case-sensitive against scheme and aliases): calls an agent or a capability in Nexus. An AigentChat-shaped nexus://<org>/<agent> (the executor removed in 2.819.0) is atlas_operation_unknown. Codes keep the atlas_ prefix. Providers are agent (the one resource is run) and capability (the resource is a capability reference). All findings are ERRORS, field = the step (loop sub-steps use the composite step id and the sub-step path). Templated executors, unparsable URLs and other schemes are skipped. A literal agent and literal capabilities keep a step from being steered by data: query.agent and every string anywhere in query.capabilities and query.model may not contain templateActionOpen, while prompt, inputs and capability args may. agent, prompt and prompt_template count as present only when they are non-empty strings after trimming whitespace. A message format takes the quoted step id first. A URL the shared executor-URL shape refuses (a dot or colon in a reference, say) is still judged here, split at the first slash after the scheme.

operationUnknown.messageFormat: step %s uses %s, which is not a Nexus operation. The providers are agent (resource run) and capability (resource: a capability reference).

agentMissing.messageFormat: step %s runs a Nexus agent but query.agent is missing, empty or not a string.
agentMissing.suggestion: Set query.agent to the agent to run, written out as a literal such as @acme/reporter.

agentNotLiteral.messageFormat: step %s computes query.agent from a template. The agent must be a fixed literal, never derived from input.
agentNotLiteral.suggestion: Write the agent out as a literal such as @acme/reporter. Data may go into the prompt or the inputs instead.

capabilitiesNotLiteral.messageFormat: step %s computes an entry of query.capabilities from a template. Capabilities must be fixed literals, never derived from input.
capabilitiesNotLiteral.suggestion: Write each capability out as a literal. Data may go into the prompt or the inputs instead.

promptMissing.messageFormat: step %s runs a Nexus agent with neither query.prompt nor query.prompt_template.
promptMissing.suggestion: Set exactly one of query.prompt or query.prompt_template.

promptBoth.messageFormat: step %s sets both query.prompt and query.prompt_template.
promptBoth.suggestion: Keep exactly one of query.prompt or query.prompt_template.

capabilityRefInvalid.messageFormat: step %s uses nexus://capability/%s, which is not a valid capability reference.
capabilityRefInvalid.suggestion: A capability reference starts with a letter or digit and continues with letters, digits, _ and - up to 128 characters in all.

modelNotLiteral.messageFormat: step %s computes a value of query.model from a template. The provider, model and reasoning_effort must be fixed literals, never derived from input.
modelNotLiteral.suggestion: Write the model choice out as literals. Data may go into the prompt or the inputs instead.

paramRefused.messageFormat: step %s sets %s under query. Atlas decides these itself, so a step may not set them.
paramRefused.suggestion: Remove these keys from the query.

reservedInputNames.$comment: reserved_input_name (ERROR): an input the flow declares under the top-level query: map, or as an input_schema field name, that starts with prefix. The platform keeps that namespace for values it writes itself (the acting person, the credential manifest, the untrusted-input marker); a value or default written under such a name is never delivered. Every name the platform reserves today starts with the prefix. Matching is exact and case-sensitive: one leading underscore is an ordinary name. Findings carry no step id. queryFieldFormat takes the input name; schemaFieldFormat takes the field name as written (a non-string name is skipped). Query names are reported sorted, then schema fields in file order.
reservedInputNames.messageFormat: the input %s starts with two underscores. That namespace belongs to the platform (the acting person, the credential manifest, the untrusted-input marker): a flow cannot declare an input there, and a value or default written under such a name is never delivered.
reservedInputNames.suggestion: Rename the input so it does not start with "__".

flowDataReservedKeys.$comment: flow_data_key_reserved (ERROR, no loop demotion): a key of the top-level data: map (the flow's pre-populated state) that names engine state. data: is seeded into the mission's .data namespace, where the engine keeps its own bookkeeping, so such a key would forge internal state. A key is reserved when it equals an entry of exact (case-sensitive) or starts with a prefix entry; the first match supplies the reason text. Field format: fieldFormat with the key. Reference: FlowDataKeyReservation / validateFlowDataKeysAreNotReserved (AIgentFlow v2.828.0). Order of exact and prefixes is the reference's lookup order.

exact.org_id: the mission's organization, set by the engine for Thalamus/Engram calls
exact.orchestrator: the removed orchestrator's state namespace (a pre-2.838.0 mission may still carry it)

prefixes.reason: keys starting with `_` are engine bookkeeping (current flow, loop and for_each context, taint lists such as `__untrusted_*`)
keys starting with `.` are engine step-response slots
the `memory.` namespace belongs to the engine
the `orchestrator.` namespace belonged to the orchestrator (removed in 2.838.0); a pre-2.838.0 mission may still carry it
the `campaign.` namespace belongs to the campaign engine
the `voiceagent.` namespace belongs to the voice agent

flowDataReservedKeys.messageFormat: data: key %q is reserved: %s. It would write into the engine's own state, so it is not seeded.
flowDataReservedKeys.suggestion: Rename the key (no leading `_` or `.`, and not one of the engine namespaces memory., orchestrator., campaign., voiceagent.).

functionOperations.$comment: unknown_function_operation (ERROR, no loop demotion): a step or loop sub-step whose executor is function://<provider>/<resource> where <provider>/<resource> is not one of the built-ins registered in the reference binary (a closed, compile-time set; nothing is loaded at run time). Templated executors, unparsable URLs and other schemes are skipped. Field: the step's executor field. Reference: validateFunctionOperationKnown (AIgentFlow v2.831.0).
functionOperations.messageFormat: step %q uses function://%s, which is not a built-in function. Available: %s
functionOperations.suggestion: Use one of the built-in functions: %s.

serverOwnedQueryKeys.$comment: Executor parameters only the server's credential resolver may set. A key in keys, matched exactly and case-sensitively, is refused (error) in the query of a top-level step (field stepFieldFormat) and of a loop sub-step (field loopStepFieldFormat, whose second placeholder is the sub-step's id as written). No other surface is scanned. A new server-owned key is a change to keys. Reference: validateNoServerOwnedStepQueryKeys, IsServerOwnedParamKey (CFX-05, after v2.790.0).

credentialEndpointPairing.$comment: credential_endpoint_unpaired (WARNING, never an error): the one statically certain shape of AIgentFlow's run-time credential/endpoint pairing refusal. ai: an ai://<provider>/... step (top-level or loop sub-step) whose query holds a non-empty string <provider>+providerBaseUrlParamSuffix while neither its query (genericKeyParam or <provider>+providerKeyParamSuffix, non-empty strings) nor executor_config.<provider>.api_key (a literal, not an env reference) supplies a key; and executor_config.<provider>.base_url for a provider in executorConfigProviders when it is a literal, the block has no literal api_key, and it is not the case that at least one step uses the provider and every such step brings its own query key. keylessProviders are exempt from both. families: a step whose executor resolves (the key protocol+familyKeySeparator+driver, else protocol) to a row. implicitServerCredential rows are never judged. A row warns when its secret (the first non-empty string secretParam in the query, else per configKey in order: executor_config api_key when configApiKeyParam is a secretParam, else the first non-empty string secretParam under extra) is exactly an env reference to a serverEnv name on a row with expandsServerEnvReferences, and its endpoint (the first non-empty string endpointParam in the query, else per configKey: base_url when configBaseUrlParam is an endpointParam, else the first non-empty string endpointParam under extra) is a literal: no templateActionOpen, not an env reference, and not of the same origin as a defaultEndpoint (lower-cased scheme://host:port, defaultPorts filled). serverEnv is the reference's per-family server-variable set, evaluated. Field formats are the reference's. Reference: validateCredentialEndpointPairing (DC-FORGE-231) and validateFamilyCredentialEndpointPairing (DC-FORGE-233).

complianceResidency.$comment: compliance_residency_unenforced (WARNING, never an error; needs no catalogue). When compliance.residency is non-empty and every code (trimmed, upper-cased) is in euResidencyCodes, each top-level step and loop sub-step whose executor starts with aiProtocol+protocolSeparator warns when its provider (literal, lower-cased; skipped when empty or containing templateActionOpen) is in regionLaneProviders and the call is not pinned. Pinned = query region a non-empty string after trimming; OR enforce_region true (bool true or the strings in enforceRegionTrueStrings); OR the author named the endpoint: query <provider>+baseUrlParamSuffix a non-empty string after trimming, or executor_config.<provider>.base_url non-empty after trimming. The provider segment of ai://<provider>/<operation> exists only when a slash follows it. regionLaneProviders is the set of providers whose adapter routes on `region`; a provider outside it has no region lane and is never warned. Message, suggestion and site formats fill %s and %q (a Go-quoted string) in order; the message's last placeholder is the residency list as written, printed [A B]. Reference: validateResidencyEnforcement (validation.residency.go).
complianceResidency.messageFormat: %s calls provider %q, whose default endpoint commits to no jurisdiction, but sets neither region nor enforce_region, so nothing pins it to the declared residency %v. compliance.residency is a catalogue eligibility check, not endpoint evidence
complianceResidency.suggestion: Add `region: eu` and `enforce_region: true` to the call. Prove it afterwards: the step record's diagnostics.region is stamped from the host actually dialled.

examples.$comment: The examples: block. Derived from the reference's constants, never hand-typed: limits, vocabularies, the credential-shaped-literal pattern set and each code's severity. example_ref_blocked_host is listed for completeness but is raised by the reference implementation only; the ports never raise it. See PARITY.md, 'The examples block'.

knownKeys.$comment: Derived by reflection over the reference's Flow type, following yaml.v3's field rules (yaml tag, lowercased field name, inline structs merged). KnownFields(true) refuses any key a struct type does not declare. A shape is scalar | any | map<S> | list<S> | a type name below. any is never inspected (a Go interface, or a type with its own unmarshaller). How it is derived and checked, and how to regenerate it: PARITY.md, 'Unknown keys and value kinds'.
